note: Eight non-coding categories for studying, protocols, planning and information management. Wired in 2026-10-29: the live list is ai-chat-panel/lib/work-context-categories.json and the live icons are ai-chat-panel/media/context-icons/. SVGs for these are in docs/plans/context-icons-proposed/.

categories.label: Studying
categories.example: Quiz me on thermodynamics for Friday's exam.
categories.description: Learning or revising course material: explaining concepts, working through exercises, exam preparation, quizzes and flashcards.

categories.label: Notes and minutes
categories.example: Turn my meeting notes into minutes with action items.
categories.description: Meeting minutes, lab or session protocols, logs and journals, and summarizing or extracting key points from a given text.

categories.label: Organizing
categories.example: Suggest a folder structure and naming scheme for my project archive.
categories.description: Structuring information: notes, files and folders, naming schemes, tags, archives and personal knowledge bases.

categories.label: Schedule and tasks
categories.example: Spread my thesis tasks over the next six weeks.
categories.description: Calendars, deadlines, to-do lists, routines and time management; excludes planning what to build.

categories.label: Math and numbers
categories.example: Work out the confidence interval for these measurements.
categories.description: Calculations, math problems, statistics, units, formulas and spreadsheet or data analysis; excludes database work.

categories.label: Language
categories.symbol: Two speech bubbles, A and script
categories.example: Translate this paragraph into German and fix the grammar.
categories.description: Translating, proofreading, rephrasing and grammar of existing text, and learning languages; writing a new document is writing.

categories.label: Ideas
categories.example: Give me ten names for the app and weigh the best three.
categories.description: Brainstorming, naming, creative writing and weighing options to reach a decision.

categories.label: Everyday life
categories.example: Which form do I need to register the move?
categories.description: Everyday matters: forms and paperwork, money, travel, shopping, health and other personal decisions.

adjustsExisting.description: Writing or revising guides, explanations, emails, letters, reports and other new text as the deliverable.
Finding documentation, facts, files, products or external information; excludes studying course material and deciding an implementation architecture.
Architecture, tradeoffs, specifications, task decomposition and discussing what to build; excludes calendars and to-do lists.

budget.method: Offline: lib/work-context.js loaded with the 24-category manifest and these description tweaks, payloads built with buildPayload(), tokens estimated as the code does (bytes / 3, about 15% above real). Clef Flash costs 3,455 Neurons per million input tokens and nothing for output. No network calls.
budget.requiredLimitChange: LIMITS.inputTokens in lib/work-context.js must go from 1500 to 2000. At 1500 the 24-category payload no longer fits (the budget left after the router's 256-token margin is 1,244), buildPayload returns null and no icon is ever chosen.
budget.perDay: About 250 classifications fit under the feature's own 1,000-Neuron cap (about 125 if every call hit the worst-case reservation); that is at most 10% of the 10,000 free Neurons per day. The 8,000 shared stop and the stop-when-spent behaviour are unchanged.
budget.tradeoff: At 2000 a long request (900 characters) leaves no room for earlier messages, so references like "do that" fall back to the current category. 2400 keeps four earlier messages for about 2 Neurons more per call.

instructionsAddition: Studying course material is study, not research; summaries and protocols are notes; calendars and to-do lists are schedule; translating or correcting existing text is language.
